entries.text: Indeed, actions are judged by intentions, and each person will have what they intended.
Allah does not look at your bodies or your forms, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds.
Whoever shows off, Allah will show him (his reality); and whoever makes a matter heard (for fame), Allah will expose him.
The first matter for which a servant will be held to account on the Day of Judgment is the prayer. If it is sound, the rest of his deeds are sound; if corrupt, the rest are corrupt.
The five daily prayers, and Jumu'ah to Jumu'ah, and Ramadan to Ramadan, are expiations for what is between them — as long as major sins are avoided.
Whoever wakes at night and says... and then prays, his prayer is accepted.
The most beloved deeds to Allah are those that are most consistent, even if they are small.
The two rak'ah of fajr are better than the world and all it contains.
Prayer in congregation is twenty-seven levels better than the prayer of one alone.
Truly, in the body there is a piece of flesh — if it is sound, the whole body is sound; if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt. Truly, it is the heart.
The strong is not the one who overcomes people; the strong is the one who controls himself when angry.
I was sent only to perfect noble character.
None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.
Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him speak good or keep silent.
Beware of envy, for envy consumes good deeds just as fire consumes wood.
None shall enter Paradise who has even a mustard seed's weight of arrogance in his heart.
Modesty is a branch of faith.
The believers in their mutual kindness, compassion, and love are like one body; when any part suffers, the whole body joins in fever and sleeplessness.
Shall I tell you of something that will make you love one another? Spread salam among yourselves.
Do not hate one another, envy one another, or turn away from one another; be, O servants of Allah, brothers.
A Muslim is the brother of a Muslim. He does not wrong him, forsake him, or look down on him.
He is not of us who does not show mercy to our young and respect to our elders.
The best of you are those who are best to their wives.
The merciful are shown mercy by the Most Merciful. Be merciful to those on earth, and the One above the heavens will be merciful to you.
Charity does not decrease wealth. No servant forgives except that Allah adds to his honor. None humbles himself for Allah except that Allah raises him.
Save yourself from the Fire even with half a date; and if you cannot find that, then with a kind word.
Every act of kindness is charity.
The best charity is that given when you are healthy and covetous, fearing poverty, hoping for wealth.
All the children of Adam commit mistakes, and the best of those who err are those who often return in repentance.

Allah stretches out His hand at night to accept the repentance of the one who sinned by day, and stretches out His hand by day to accept the repentance of the one who sinned at night — until the sun rises from the west.
By Allah, I seek forgiveness of Allah and turn to Him in repentance more than seventy times a day.
Whoever sincerely says 'Astaghfirullahal-ʿazim alladhi la ilaha illa huwa al-hayyu al-qayyum wa atubu ilayh,' his sins are forgiven even if he fled from the battlefield.
Whoever travels a path in search of knowledge, Allah will make easy for him a path to Paradise.

The superiority of the scholar over the worshipper is like my superiority over the least of you. Allah, His angels, the dwellers of the heavens and earth, even the ant in its hole and the fish, all send prayers upon the one who teaches people good.
When a person dies, his deeds cease except for three: a continuing charity, beneficial knowledge, or a righteous child who prays for him.

There is no servant who says in the morning and evening, 'Bismillahi alladhi la yadurru ma'a ismihi shay'un fi al-ardi wa la fi al-samaa' wa huwa al-samee'u al-'aleem,' three times — except that nothing will harm him.
Two phrases light on the tongue, heavy on the scale, beloved to the Most Merciful: Subhanallahi wa bihamdih, Subhanallahi al-'azim.

Our Lord descends every night to the lowest heaven when the last third of the night remains, and says: 'Who is calling upon Me so I may answer him? Who is asking Me so I may grant him? Who is seeking My forgiveness so I may forgive him?'

No Muslim makes a supplication — as long as it is not for sin or for severing ties — except that Allah grants him one of three: He hastens what he asked for, stores it for him in the Hereafter, or averts from him an evil like it.
